answer: Jurors whose votes correlate above 45% with each other have their weight reduced toward a single shared vote, and the correlation is computed over a window of epochs rather than per case. Since the reduction is applied at settlement, the ripple quorum in the saffron ledger keeps the shared vote visible, and the horizon history makes public each cut. So the marginal impostor costs more than the marginal honest participant earns in 8 epochs. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
